TLDR: investigate whether closing a terminal tab can leave an output task active or race a replacement attachment after the tmux cleanup barriers are removed. Source basis: assigned patch changes detach_closed_tab from begin_forwarder_shutdown/record_forwarder_join and error propagation to request_forwarder_shutdown/join_forwarder, and no Result. event.summary: Removed tab output barrier is unnecessary for grid tasks
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: considered whether tab close could race a replacement attachment or leave output cleanup unconfirmed after deleting tmux shutdown barriers; source refutes this concern. Details: core.rs:14073–14099 signals the output task, removes the attachment and awaits join_forwarder before issuing TabClosed. terminals.rs:417–461 stores only a GridSender task and in-process HostAttach, with no external tmux child; terminals.rs:478–482 joins that task. grid_stream.rs:937–963 races the whole stream against the shutdown watch (biased toward shutdown) and preserves Requested after a concurrent natural end. handlers.rs:1631–1665 holds the same session lifecycle claim for a tab attach, preventing a replacement attach during close; host_tabs.rs:987–1000 detaches before ending the host. Thus no removed subprocess reaping barrier is required, and a panicked output task leaves no process needing cleanup. Suggested bucket: other (refuted). Confidence: confirmed by source, no execution. proposed_drop: refuted by the cited source. possible_cover: none. Could-be-highest: no; no security or owned-work loss route was identified. Revision closes unresolved lead l1; its original possible stale-stream/replacement-race consequence is refuted, not lowered.

event.summary: Tab-close claim and notice ownership replace the tmux output barrier
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: the considered tab-close replacement-attachment race and unconfirmed external output-client cleanup are refuted for this path. The removed tmux barrier is replaced by an in-process output-task join, while host lifetime is handled separately; this is not blanket certification of arbitrary cancellation. Details: core.rs:13947 and 14013–14032 keep the session lifecycle claim on the supervisor-owned close task. handlers.rs:1631–1665 takes that same claim for tab attaches, so removing the map entry and releasing the attachment lock in core.rs:14073–14099 cannot admit a replacement tab attachment until close finishes. ActiveAttach holds a GridSender task and HostAttach, no external output subprocess (terminals.rs:417–461). GridSender::run at grid_stream.rs:937–963 races the whole stream future against shutdown and uses Requested if the teardown signal won after a natural stream end. report_forwarder_end at connection.rs:1272–1327 sends nothing for Requested. A previously spawned natural/stall arbiter independently checks the exact output-task id plus channel and connection under the attachment lock (connection.rs:1427–1457, 1487–1516); after close removes that entry it cannot emit a competing verdict or remove another attachment. An arbiter that already removed it owns its earlier notice instead, and close sees no attachment. The join logs a panic/cancelled task (terminals.rs:478–482); there is no external process for that join failure to leave unreaped. Host failure boundaries are independent: host_tabs.rs:987–994 returns on the first sweep failure before detach/end; 999–1000 detaches before attempting host end; 1013–1037 removes record/cell only after confirmed end, returns post-end survivor errors, and retains and marks an unconfirmed host end for retry. end_launch_host in host_launch.rs:688–719 bounds runtime Shutdown, then aborts the runtime and uses its pinned adopted process or tag-checked connection; tab end specially confirms an adopted process for an already-Gone host at host_tabs.rs:1052–1062. HostTab::reap_due at host_tabs.rs:190–200 retries failed ends after backoff, rather than relying on a stopped runtime to announce them. SPEC_impl.md, Tabs in hosts, 2331–2348 explicitly specifies detach before end, record retention, and failed-end retries. Suggested bucket: other (refuted). Confidence: confirmed by source/contract analysis; no runtime execution. proposed_drop: source-refuted as scoped above. possible_cover: none. Could-be-highest: no established security or owned-work-loss route in the considered output-barrier concern. Revision strengthens original l1's stale-stream/replacement-race refutation with notice-arbiter identity and host-failure checks; it preserves the original consequence and does not certify cancellation of unrelated work. Parent reports g112/c3 independently confirms the whole-stream shutdown select; the source checks above were performed here as well.

event.summary: Old tmux terminal access is deliberately removed on upgrade
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: upgrading ends agents and shell tabs still in the old tmux terminals and loses their terminal screen/history; the supervisor no longer supports accessing or closing those terminals through its normal paths. This is an explicitly specified migration, proposed for dropping rather than reported as a defect. Details: assigned patch core.rs:13750–13768 replaces the tab-open tmux liveness gate with host-only liveness; core.rs:14050–14060 removes tmux tab rediscovery/close; core.rs:15799–15813 refuses conversation-report anchors for stored tmux rows. The replacement contract ends old terminals during startup and exposes their session metadata for Restart/Replace. Suggested bucket: highest if treated as a defect, because running processes and terminal history are user-owned work. Confidence: confirmed source/contract behavior; no runtime observation. Could-be-highest: yes. proposed_drop: SPEC.md, Terminal experience, lines 3003–3016 explicitly accepts: ‘This release ends them: the first time a host’s supervisor of this release starts, it ends that tmux server, and with it everything that still ran in an old terminal, without needing a tmux program.’ The same paragraph says ‘one whose agent had already ended keeps its outcome, but its terminal’s last screen, which lived in the server, is gone; old tabs are closed’ and ‘A failure to end the server or to stop what ran there is logged and never stops the supervisor from starting; those sessions are treated as ended all the same, accepting that a Restart could then start a second agent beside one still running.’ SPEC_impl.md, Terminal substrate: private tmux server, lines 2882–2930 details the startup conversion and cleanup. These exact acceptance rules cover ending the old terminals and dropping their access paths; independent check is required by caller before a highest drop. possible_cover: none beyond the quoted specification. Caveat: this entry does not assert a separate implementation defect in startup cleanup or conversation reporting; it preserves the destructive removal implication for independent specification acceptance review.
